blockers.title: Historical RETURN ignores disagreement between immutable P9 Agent identity and fresh Auth identity

source.obligation: Each successor chain uses exact Auth UUID/type/status/agent_id and documented historical binding; every non-null identity assertion must agree; identity mismatch rejects the whole new business write.

blockers.counterexample: An exact prior P responsibility exists in the same Instance/node. Its immutable P9 row maps P to Q with canonical_agent_id=agt_original. Q is a local enabled AGENT with no second edge. Fresh Auth returns exact Q, active, agentId=agt_different and Agent directory returns that exact different ID with exists/enabled true. resolve_current_principal drops all P9 metadata, observe accepts the new pair, and RETURN appends a Q Visit despite the contradictory identity chain. Both Agent IDs can satisfy the canonical grammar; no display-name inference or hypothetical network forgery is needed. The implementation has no comparison that can reject this state.
blockers.support: The existing new positive historical_return_persists_validated_q_preserving_p_and_original_request fixture records canonical-{q} at tests/31_admission_wiring.rs:1018, while the directory stub returns agent-{q} at :120, and expects success at :1120-1132. Its 9/0 executed suite is hash-verified; reviewer did not execute a new counterexample.
blockers.impact: The new historical bridge can create a responsibility using a fresh Agent binding inconsistent with the immutable evidence used to select Q, rather than failing closed on ambiguous/corrupt/drifted evidence. UUID-only validity is not proof that all identity assertions agree. This affects T1 source readiness and is independent of T3 DTO semantics.

Keep old P disabled acceptance, Q disabled/missing/unavailable denial, raw request/hash/actor and replay behavior. No new identity service, grant, migration membership, API or Spec amendment is needed for this comparison.
